Syntax
An array can be created using the array() language construct. It takes any number
of comma-separated key => value pairs as arguments.
array(
key => value,
key2 => value2,
key3 => value3,
...
)

<?php

questions.stem: Which statement is false about modern JavaScript running in a browser sandbox?

options.label: A
options.text: The language cannot support sophisticated applications

options.label: B
options.text: Scripts can access selected client devices through permission-based APIs

options.label: C
options.text: Scripts have restricted access to arbitrary client files and hardware

options.label: D
options.text: Script source can be supplied as text and executed by the browser

questions.hint: Check exact language syntax, declaration rules and execution context before reasoning about the result.
sources: MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · 2016 · Question 75

answer.text: The language cannot support sophisticated applications
answer.explanation: Browser JavaScript supports sophisticated applications; its sandbox is a restriction on access to resources, not proof of an inherently weak language. Selected file or device access can be exposed through permission-based APIs, while arbitrary hardware access remains restricted. JavaScript source can be included in pages or loaded from a script file. Thus the language-capability claim is false, while the qualified environment and source-delivery claims are compatible.

choices.explanation: The note explicitly allows sophisticated applications, so this denial is false.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Permission-based APIs allow selected device access.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Script inclusion supplies source for browser execution.

evidence.quote: Browser scripts are sandboxed, but may access selected files/devices through permission-based APIs.
They are not inherently limited to trivial programs, nor can they freely access arbitrary client hardware.

answer.explanation: WEB05 defines HTTPS as HTTP over TLS, protecting channel confidentiality and integrity and authenticating the server through certificate checks. That is the secure web-communication protocol among the main choices. Plain HTTP, FTP, and TCP/IP do not by their names supply that TLS-protected web exchange. The alternate option set places HTTPS at C, so its answer letter differs.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: FTP is not the HTTPS protocol for TLS-protected web communication identified in the note.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: TCP/IP names underlying networking protocols rather than the TLS-protected HTTP scheme requested.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS and supplies the channel protections described in WEB05.

evidence.quote: HTTPS uses HTTP over TLS, protecting channel confidentiality/integrity and authenticating the server under certificate checks.

The Document Object Model (DOM) is the data representation of the objects that

Model (DOM) is a programming interface for web documents. It represents the page
so that programs can change the document structure, style, and content. The DOM
represents the document as nodes and objects; that way, programming languages can
interact with the page.

getElementsByTagName(tag) returns elements with the given tag name
- querySelector(selector) → The Document method querySelector() returns
the first Element within the document that matches the specified selector,
or group of selectors. If no matches are found, null is returned.

questions.stem: Which situations demonstrate concurrency when their requests make overlapping progress? Here simultaneously means overlapping progress, not necessarily execution at the same instant. Select all that apply.

options.label: A
options.text: The ability of the server to handle multiple clients simultaneously

options.label: B
options.text: The ability of the client to handle multiple servers simultaneously

options.label: C
options.text: The ability of the server to handle multiple requests from a single client

options.label: D
options.text: The ability of the client to handle multiple requests to a single server

questions.hint: Identify the execution side and communication pattern, keeping runtime, transport, data format and callback roles distinct.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 117

answer.text: The ability of the server to handle multiple clients simultaneously; The ability of the client to handle multiple servers simultaneously; The ability of the server to handle multiple requests from a single client; The ability of the client to handle multiple requests to a single server
answer.explanation: Concurrency means overlapping progress, whereas parallelism requires execution at the same instant. A server can overlap work for several clients or several requests from one client. A client can likewise overlap interactions with several servers or multiple requests to one server. The question explicitly supplies overlap for each situation, making every listed arrangement an example of concurrency without asserting that all work physically runs in parallel.

choices.explanation: Overlapping server work for several clients is concurrent.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Overlapping client interactions with several servers are concurrent.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Several overlapping requests from one client can create server concurrency.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A client can overlap multiple requests to the same server.

questions.hint: Identify the shared-state invariant and the operations that must be coordinated.

answer.text: Shared-resource correctness depends on execution interleaving.
answer.explanation: WEB37 describes two requests reading stock one, both accepting a sale, and both writing zero. The final correctness depends on their interleaving, which is the race-condition mechanism captured most closely by C’s unpredictable shared-resource access. Competing connections, multiple responders, or duplicate requests are not themselves sufficient; they become races only when shared-state correctness depends on timing.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Competition to establish a connection is not by itself a shared-state correctness failure caused by interleaving.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Several servers responding does not alone establish a race on shared mutable state.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the closest option: shared-state access can make correctness depend on the execution interleaving.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Duplicate requests can cause other problems, but duplication alone is not the defining race-condition mechanism.

evidence.quote: Suppose two requests read a stock count1, both decide it is available and both write0: two sales consumed one item.

questions.stem: Which technique directly protects one shared-state critical section with an exclusive lock that does not rely on busy waiting? Choose the exclusive-lock primitive, rather than a bounded-access counter or a messaging design.
questions.hint: Identify the shared-state invariant and the operations that must be coordinated.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 119

answer.explanation: A mutex directly protects a critical section by allowing only one holder at a time. The question distinguishes that exclusive-lock abstraction from spinlock busy waiting, semaphore bounded-access counting and message-queue designs. A semaphore can also enforce exclusion when configured suitably, but it is not the specific exclusive-lock primitive requested. Choosing a primitive does not by itself guarantee application correctness: every conflicting update must use the protected critical section.

choices.explanation: A mutex is the requested exclusive-lock primitive.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A spinlock relies on busy waiting, which the stem excludes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A semaphore is the bounded-access counter abstraction excluded by the requested category.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A message queue is a messaging design rather than the requested lock primitive.

evidence.quote: A mutex protects one critical section; semaphores can coordinate bounded access; spinlocks busy-wait and are unsuitable for blocking a browser/event-loop thread.

evidence.quote: Resetting nav ul with list-style-type:none; margin:0; padding:0 removes bullets and default spacing only; it does not itself arrange links horizontally or create a dropdown.

questions.stem: Which PHP superglobal is dedicated to URL query parameters, excluding configurable combined-source arrays?
questions.hint: Identify the data source or security responsibility precisely, and check whether a combined source or a different control could also qualify.

answer.explanation: $_GET is the dedicated query-parameter source. $_REQUEST can also contain GET values depending on configuration, but it is a combined-source array and is explicitly excluded by this question. $_POST represents supported form POST data, while isset tests existence and non-null rather than acting as an input-data container. Removing placeholder brackets makes the array names clear without inventing a particular field name or request value.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This combines configured request sources rather than being dedicated to query parameters.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This is the supported form POST source.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: This is the dedicated URL-query source.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: This tests whether a variable or entry exists and is non-null.

evidence.quote: $_GET contains query parameters; $_POST contains supported form POST data; $_FILES upload metadata; $_SERVER request/environment details; $_COOKIE cookie values; $_SESSION session data after startup.
$_REQUEST may combine GET/POST/cookie data according to configuration; it is not a database interface and has ambiguous precedence, so prefer the intended source.
isset tests existence and non-null, not truth or valid syntax.

questions.stem:
____________is a service that allows organizations and individuals to post a website or a 
web page onto the Internet.
questions.hint: Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

answer.explanation: WEB02 defines hosting as supplying the environment where a website is served. This is the service enabling an organization’s site or page to be made available online. An ISP supplies connectivity, domain registration reserves a name, and a web client requests resources. Those supporting roles are not the hosting service described.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Hosting supplies an environment in which the site is served to users.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: An ISP provides connectivity rather than necessarily the environment serving the website.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A web client requests resources instead of providing the publishing environment.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Domain registration reserves a name rather than serving the site’s content.

evidence.quote: Hosting supplies an environment where a site is served; domain registration reserves a name, and DNS maps names to network records.
An ISP provides connectivity.

questions.stem:
Which protocol is mostly used for communication between client and server in a web 
application?
questions.hint: Identify the protocol layer and the intended request, response or channel semantics.

answer.explanation: WEB01 describes the Web as a resource system commonly using HTTP, and WEB03 details its request/response exchange. HTTPS adds TLS protection to HTTP but does not make one of the other offered protocols the ordinary web exchange. Among these choices, HTTP is the application protocol used to request and return web resources.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: FTP is not the HTTP request/response web protocol described in the note.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: SMTP is not the webpage request/response protocol developed in WEB03.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: HTTP carries the web resource requests and responses described in the complete note.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: SSH is not the ordinary webpage request/response protocol identified here.

evidence.quote: The Internet connects networks; the Web is a resource system commonly using HTTP.
An HTTP/1.1 request begins with method, request-target and version, followed by header fields, a blank line, and an optional body.
HTTP defines web application requests, response status codes and representations.
An HTTP exchange can use underlying TCP connections and IP addresses; naming that network stack does not identify the application-level method or status semantics.
FTP is a file-transfer application protocol.
SMTP transports electronic mail.

questions.stem: What is the extension of JavaScript file?
questions.hint: Check exact language syntax, declaration rules and execution context before reasoning about the result.

answer.text: .js is the conventional JavaScript source extension.
answer.explanation: WEB15 uses an external app.js script and explicitly calls it a .js file. B identifies that extension family despite its uppercase printed letters. Actual filename case must match the deployed resource where paths are case-sensitive; the conventional spelling is lowercase .js. The other choices name different or invented file extensions rather than JavaScript source.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The invented .javaS suffix is not the conventional .js extension specified by WEB15.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: This identifies the JS extension; use conventional lowercase .js and preserve actual filename case in paths.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: .java is not the .js source-file extension used for JavaScript in the note.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: CSS identifies stylesheet source rather than the JavaScript file extension.

evidence.quote: Use <script src="app.js"></script> for an external .js file; script content has no HTML closing-tag syntax inside its JavaScript source.
JavaScript originated at Netscape; it is distinct from Java and supports sophisticated applications through prototype-based objects and first-class functions.

questions.stem: A web application has two protected endpoints. The profile endpoint checks a valid session identifier and its server-side user record on every request. The transfer endpoint grants access whenever the editable logged_in cookie equals 1 and ignores session validation. An unauthenticated attacker has no valid session and sets logged_in=1. Which result follows from these access checks?

options.label: A
options.text: The cookie edit can bypass the transfer endpoint, but does not grant access to the profile endpoint

options.label: B
options.text: The cookie edit grants access to both endpoints because both receive the same cookie

options.label: C
options.text: Neither endpoint can be bypassed unless the attacker first obtains a genuine session identifier

options.label: D
options.text: HTTPS alone prevents either endpoint from accepting a forged logged_in value

questions.hint: Follow the identifier and server-side state through the stated lifecycle or access check; distinguish client-controlled claims from server decisions.

answer.text: The cookie edit can bypass the transfer endpoint, but does not grant access to the profile endpoint
answer.explanation: The two endpoints use different trust paths. The transfer endpoint trusts an attacker-controlled flag, so the forged value satisfies its stated access check without a valid session. The profile endpoint requires authenticated server-side state, which the attacker lacks, so the unrelated cookie does not grant access there. HTTPS protects transport rather than validating the truth of a client-generated login claim. The bypass therefore affects the transfer endpoint only.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Only the transfer endpoint relies solely on the forgeable flag; the profile endpoint still requires a valid session.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Receiving the same cookie does not make the endpoints apply the same authorization rule.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The transfer check requires no genuine session identifier, so stealing one is unnecessary for that bypass.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: HTTPS does not prevent a client from submitting a false authorization flag.

evidence.quote: A client cookie logged_in=1 is attacker-controlled.
If the server trusts it alone, authorization can be bypassed.
If the server checks a valid session ID and its server-side user/role on every protected action, editing that unrelated flag does not grant rights.
HTTPS does not make client-generated claims trustworthy.

questions.stem: Why should form <input> elements include an associated <label> with the for attribute?

options.label: D
options.text: It improves accessibility: screen readers announce the label when the input is focused

questions.hint: Separate the control role, displayed content, submitted value and form destination.

answer.text: Provide an accessible label associated with the input.
answer.explanation: WEB09 links a label’s for to the control id, and WEB07 requires programmatic control labels. That association lets assistive technology identify the input and announce its label. It does not alter storage, encryption, or network submission speed. D states the accessibility purpose directly, rather than confusing it with unrelated browser or transport features.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Label association does not create offline storage for form values.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Labels do not encrypt data or replace HTTPS transport protection.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Associating a label does not accelerate form submission over the network.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The programmatic label identifies the focused input for screen readers and other assistive technology.

evidence.quote: A label’s for matches the control’s id; name identifies its submitted field.
Give controls programmatic labels, clear link text and keyboard access; visual styling alone does not establish accessibility.

questions.stem: What is the difference between GET and POST methods? When would you use each?
questions.hint: Identify the protocol layer and the intended request, response or channel semantics.

answer.text: GET retrieves safely and usually places form values in the query; POST asks the target to process body content.
answer.explanation: WEB04 recommends GET for reading representations rather than intentional state changes. POST suits submitted processing or actions such as enrollment with proper authorization and CSRF controls. Neither method encrypts data; use HTTPS for channel protection. POST body values remain visible to tools and subject to configured size limits rather than becoming secret or unlimited.

evidence.quote: GET retrieves a representation with safe semantics; do not implement an intentional state-changing action as a GET link.
POST asks the target to process supplied content.
GET forms usually put name/value pairs in the URL query; POST forms put them in the body.
For an enrollment action use POST with CSRF controls, server authorization, capacity checks and a transaction; show success only after commit.

questions.stem: Why is client-side validation alone not enough for security?
questions.hint: Separate event dispatch, handler registration and cancellation of the browser default action.

answer.text: Clients can bypass or alter browser checks, so the server must validate and authorize again.
answer.explanation: WEB27 requires server checks for required fields, type, length, and range, plus authentication and authorization before processing. Browser validation improves feedback but arbitrary clients can submit different requests. Bind SQL values and encode output for its context as well; encryption or merely connecting to a database does not replace these application controls.

evidence.quote: Read input, check required fields/type/length/range, authenticate and authorize, then process.
Bind SQL parameters to keep values separate from commands.
Encode output for HTML/attribute/JS context; textContent handles plain browser text.
Browser checks improve feedback; repeat validation and authorization on the server.

questions.stem: What is the DOM and why is it important for web development?
questions.hint: Track which node is selected or created, and distinguish changing content from attaching a node.

answer.text: The DOM is the document’s node hierarchy, enabling scripts to inspect and update page content and behavior.
answer.explanation: WEB20 selects nodes, creates elements, and attaches them to that hierarchy. Creating a node does not itself insert it, and missing lookups must be guarded. textContent safely inserts untrusted plain text, whereas innerHTML reparses markup and can replace descendant state. The DOM connects document structure to interactive browser updates.

evidence.quote: The DOM is a hierarchy of nodes representing the document.
Creation alone does not insert it.
innerHTML parses/replaces descendants, so += reparses/replaces the prior descendant content too and can destroy listeners/state.
Use textContent for untrusted plain text.

questions.stem: A user closes their browser and reopens it. They are still logged in. How is this possible?
questions.hint: Follow the identifier and server-side state through the stated lifecycle or access check; distinguish client-controlled claims from server decisions.

answer.text: A persistent remember/session token or browser restoration can preserve the login flow.
answer.explanation: WEB28 says reopening while logged in may use persistent session or remember tokens or browser restoration. The browser can retain an identifier, but the server still has to accept and validate it against its authorization state. Local persistence alone is not proof of authenticated access, and the observation does not identify one unique storage mechanism.

evidence.quote: Being logged in after reopening may use a persistent session/remember token or browser restoration; storage alone does not prove server acceptance.
If the server checks a valid session ID and its server-side user/role on every protected action, editing that unrelated flag does not grant rights.

questions.stem: Why would a developer choose local storage over cookies?
questions.hint: Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

answer.text: localStorage persists origin data without automatically attaching it to every matching request.
answer.explanation: WEB28 contrasts localStorage’s persistent strings with cookies’ automatic request transmission. It can avoid transmitting data needed only by the client. JavaScript can still send stored tokens explicitly, so localStorage is not inherently incapable of session designs. Script-access risks and persistence policies must be considered; neither mechanism is universally preferable for sensitive authentication data.

evidence.quote: localStorage persists origin-specific string values across sessions until removed/cleared; sessionStorage is scoped to a page session/tab.
Neither is automatically transmitted like matching cookies, but JavaScript can send stored data explicitly.
Thus all four are client storage techniques, and localStorage can participate in token-based session designs, with script-access risks.

questions.stem: What does HTML stand for?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB06 directly expands HTML as HyperText Markup Language. The name identifies markup used for document structure and meaning rather than a general programming or transfer protocol. The other phrases substitute different words and are not the expansion in the note. This vocabulary answer does not depend on a browser version or an implementation choice.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Hyper Text Markup Language matches the note’s expansion, with only spacing variation in HyperText.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: High Tech Modern Language is not the expansion given in WEB06.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Transfer replaces the required word Text and gives the wrong expansion.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Home Tool Markup Language is not the HTML expansion in the note.

evidence.quote: HTML means HyperText Markup Language.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag creates a hyperlink?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB07 gives Read as the link pattern. The anchor element creates the user-facing hyperlink; href is its destination attribute, not a standalone tag. link is used for relationships such as external stylesheets, and url is not the anchor element. Thus C names the correct element among the supplied choices.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: link is used for resource relationships such as external stylesheets rather than the shown user-facing anchor.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: href is an attribute on an anchor, not the hyperlink element itself.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The anchor element with href creates the hyperlink described in WEB07.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: url is not the supported HTML anchor tag.

evidence.quote: Use Read for a link; href is the destination, not url/link.
An external sheet uses <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> in head; an internal sheet uses style; an inline declaration uses an element’s style attribute.

questions.stem: What is the correct HTML tag for inserting a line break?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation:
creates a line break,

represents a thematic break. C is the defined break element; the other options invent element names not defined as HTML elements. A line break is an HTML structure operation rather than a requirement to insert a physical newline into the source file.

choices.explanation: lb is not the supported line-break element spelling.

choices.label: C

marks paragraphs;
is a line break and

a thematic break.

questions.stem: Which tag preserves whitespace and line breaks exactly as written?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB06 gives <pre> the whitespace-preservation role. It is therefore the appropriate element for text whose source spaces and line breaks should be retained. code marks code semantics but does not itself guarantee preformatted whitespace, while paragraph and emphasis elements have other meanings. Custom CSS can alter defaults, but the question concerns the native tag role.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A paragraph does not itself preserve all source spacing and line breaks.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: pre is the element explicitly defined to preserve source whitespace.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: code marks code semantics; preformatted whitespace preservation is a separate role.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: em expresses stress emphasis rather than preformatted source layout.

evidence.quote: <pre> preserves source whitespace; <code> marks code.
<strong> indicates importance and <em> stress; <b>/<i> have other text semantics and are not identical to importance/emphasis.

questions.stem: What is the highest-level heading tag in HTML?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB06 defines heading levels h1 through h6 as a hierarchy. h1 is the highest level and h6 the lowest, regardless of CSS choices that can change their visual size. heading and h0 are not the defined heading-level tags. The answer is semantic rank, not whichever text happens to be styled largest.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: h6 is the lowest of the defined heading levels, not the highest.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: heading is not one of the defined h1–h6 heading-level tags.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: h0 is outside the defined heading levels in WEB06.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: h1 is the highest semantic heading level in the h1–h6 hierarchy.

evidence.quote: Heading levels h1–h6 express hierarchy, with h6 conventionally smallest in default styling, not a mandatory CSS size.

questions.stem: Which element is the root element of an HTML page?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB06 explicitly identifies html as the document root, with head holding metadata and body containing document content. Those two elements are inside the document rather than replacing its root. root is not the HTML tag used for this role. Thus the root-element question directly selects C.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: head holds metadata and is not the document root.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: body holds document content but is not the document’s root element.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: html is explicitly defined as the document root in WEB06.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: root is not the HTML root tag given here.

evidence.quote: <!DOCTYPE html> selects modern standards mode; <html> is the document root, <head> holds metadata, and <body> contains document content.

questions.stem: Which attribute provides alternative text for an image?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB07 gives img a src for its resource and alt for alternative text. Informative images need meaningful alternatives; decorative ones use empty alt. A title is not a replacement for alt, and a caption is separate visible context rather than the requested attribute. Therefore C names the accessibility text attribute.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: title is not a replacement for the image’s alternative-text attribute.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: src identifies the image resource rather than its alternative text.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: alt supplies the image’s alternative text, or an empty value for purely decorative images.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: caption is not the requested image alternative-text attribute.

evidence.quote: supplies source and alternative text.
Use empty alt for purely decorative images; informative images need meaningful alternatives.
Width/height reserve dimensions; title is not a replacement for alt.

questions.stem: What does target="_blank" do in a link?

options.label: A
options.text: Opens the link in the same window

options.label: B
options.text: Opens the link in a new tab or window

options.label: D
options.text: Opens the link in a parent frame

questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.text: Open a new browsing context, commonly a new tab or window.
answer.explanation: WEB07 maps _blank to a new context, _self to current, and _parent to parent. Browser preferences decide tab versus window, so B correctly allows either. The target does not close the current window or select the parent frame. This is a browsing-context request rather than a guaranteed window-management UI behavior.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: The current context is selected by _self rather than _blank.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: _blank requests a new context, with tab versus window determined by browser behavior.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The target does not request that the current window be closed.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The parent context is selected by _parent rather than _blank.

evidence.quote: target="_self" uses the current context, _blank a new context, _parent its parent and _top the top-level context.
Browser preferences determine tab versus window.

questions.stem: Which HTML tag is used for an unordered list?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB08 defines ul as unordered and ol as ordered, with li items inside either. C therefore supplies the requested container. li is only an item, and list is not the defined HTML list-container name. Presentation of markers can be changed with CSS without changing whether the element is the unordered-list structure.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: ol is an ordered-list container, not the unordered-list container requested.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: li marks an item inside a list rather than the list container itself.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: ul is explicitly the unordered-list container in WEB08.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: list is not the unordered-list element spelling defined here.

evidence.quote: Unordered <ul> and ordered <ol> contain <li> items.

questions.stem: What HTML tag defines a table row?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.explanation: WEB08 distinguishes the table element, row elements, and header/data cells. tr defines one row, while th and td are cells placed within rows. table contains the complete tabular structure. Therefore D is the row tag, independent of how many columns or spans the cells in that row occupy.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: td defines a data cell, not the containing row.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: th defines a header cell, not the containing row.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: table defines the whole table rather than one row.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: tr is the table-row element explicitly identified in WEB08.

evidence.quote: <table> contains rows <tr>, header cells <th> and data cells <td>; a td is not the table itself.

questions.stem: What does the colspan attribute do in a table?
questions.hint: Use the element or attribute meaning and document structure, rather than appearance or a similar-looking name.

answer.text: Make one cell span multiple columns.
answer.explanation: WEB08 explicitly distinguishes colspan from rowspan. colspan allocates a cell across columns, often described informally as merging cells horizontally; it does not change a column’s color or width rule. rowspan is the vertical counterpart across rows. B therefore matches, while actual placement must still account for positions already occupied by spans.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Column color is a styling concern rather than the colspan structural span.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: colspan makes one cell occupy positions across multiple columns.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Column width is not the meaning of the colspan count.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Spanning rows is rowspan, not colspan.

evidence.quote: colspan spans columns; rowspan spans rows.
Account for occupied cells before placing the next cell, and use header associations for accessible data.

questions.stem: Which meta tag is used for responsive design on mobile devices?
questions.hint: Identify the requested presentation effect and layout context before matching the property or rule.

answer.explanation: WEB06 gives viewport metadata control over mobile viewport behavior, and WEB14 includes it alongside flexible layout and media queries for responsive design. Keywords and description concern metadata for content/discoverability, while robots concerns crawler directives. The viewport entry is the relevant mobile-layout metadata; it does not replace responsive CSS by itself.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Keywords metadata does not configure the mobile viewport used for responsive layout.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Robots metadata concerns crawler handling rather than the mobile viewport.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Description summarizes the page rather than controlling mobile viewport behavior.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Viewport metadata configures mobile viewport behavior as part of responsive design.

evidence.quote: Meta charset declares encoding; description summarizes the page; viewport controls mobile viewport behavior.
Responsive design combines flexible layout, images, viewport metadata and media queries, for example @media(max-width:600px){.cards{grid-template-columns:1fr}}.
The keywords metadata name supplies terms relevant to the page, while description supplies a page summary.
Robots metadata supplies crawler indexing or search-presentation instructions.

questions.stem: Which CSS selector targets an element with id="logo"?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB11 explicitly uses #logo as an ID selector and .notice as a class selector. Thus an element whose id is logo is targeted with #logo. A bare logo would be a type selector for an element named logo, while the starred concatenation is not the stated ID syntax. D is the correct selector.

choices.explanation: .logo targets a class named logo rather than id="logo".

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Bare logo is a type selector, not the ID selector requested.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: *logo is not the defined CSS ID-selector syntax.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: #logo is the explicit ID-selector pattern supplied in WEB11.

evidence.quote: Type p selects paragraph elements, .notice selects a class, #logo an ID, h1,h2 groups selectors, nav ul selects descendants and nav>ul direct children.

questions.stem: Which CSS selector targets all elements with class="highlight"?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB11 gives a dot-prefixed name as a class selector and a hash-prefixed name as an ID selector. Applying that rule to highlight yields .highlight. A bare word selects element type, and *highlight is not the supported class syntax. The class rule can match every element carrying that class, rather than only one unique ID.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: #highlight selects an ID rather than elements with the highlight class.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: .highlight is the dot-prefixed class selector matching the requested class.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: *highlight is not the defined class-selector syntax.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Bare highlight is an element-type selector rather than a class selector.

evidence.quote: Type p selects paragraph elements, .notice selects a class, #logo an ID, h1,h2 groups selectors, nav ul selects descendants and nav>ul direct children.

questions.stem: Which method of inserting CSS allows it to apply to multiple pages?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB11 says external CSS promotes reuse and consistent design through a linked stylesheet. Multiple documents can link the same styles.css file, so one shared source applies across pages. Inline declarations belong to one element and internal/embedded style blocks belong to their document. They can be copied, but copying is not the shared-source attachment method requested.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Inline declarations belong to an element rather than one shared stylesheet linked by multiple pages.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: An internal style block belongs to its document rather than a separately shared resource.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Multiple pages can link the same external stylesheet for shared rules and maintenance.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Embedded styles are document-local rather than the shared external attachment method.

evidence.quote: An external sheet uses <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> in head; an internal sheet uses style; an inline declaration uses an element’s style attribute.
External CSS promotes reuse, consistent design and caching; it does not guarantee that every page becomes smaller or accessible.

questions.stem: What symbol is used to group multiple selectors in CSS?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB11 groups selectors using h1,h2. The comma separates alternative selectors that receive the same declaration block. Semicolons separate declarations, colons separate a property from its value or occur in pseudo syntax, and dots introduce classes. Thus C is the selector-list grouping separator, not a declaration delimiter.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Semicolons separate declarations rather than selectors in a selector list.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A colon is not the separator for grouped alternative selectors.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A comma groups selector alternatives, as in the note’s h1,h2 example.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A dot introduces a class selector rather than grouping multiple selectors.

evidence.quote: Type p selects paragraph elements, .notice selects a class, #logo an ID, h1,h2 groups selectors, nav ul selects descendants and nav>ul direct children.
A rule is selector { property: value; }.

questions.stem: What does text-decoration: underline do in CSS?
questions.hint: Identify the requested presentation effect and layout context before matching the property or rule.

answer.explanation: WEB13 assigns text-decoration effects such as underline. The specific value underline therefore adds an underline decoration. Bold uses font-weight and italic uses font-style; a strike-through is a different decoration value. The declaration changes presentation rather than the semantic importance or stress of the underlying HTML text.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Boldness is controlled by font-weight rather than the underline decoration.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Italic styling uses font-style rather than text-decoration:underline.

choices.label: C

questions.stem: What does the accept attribute on a file-upload input do?

options.label: B
options.text: Hints which file types the browser’s file picker should offer

questions.hint: Identify the role requested and compare it with the definitions and constraints in the cited passages.

answer.text: Hints which file types the browser’s file picker should offer
answer.explanation: accept is a browser selection hint describing file types the picker should offer. It does not guarantee what an attacker can submit or what the server actually accepts. Server-side validation must separately check upload errors, size and content before safe storage. The attribute also neither initiates transfer, sets a maximum upload size nor validates a filename. The choice states the UI role without claiming server enforcement.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The attribute does not validate filenames.

answer.explanation: video is the native HTML element for video, and embed and object can also embed supported resources, including multimedia in a suitable environment. Browser support, resource formats and appropriate permissions still matter; the selection describes capability rather than guaranteed playback of every resource.

questions.stem: What does session_start() do in PHP?

options.label: B
options.text: Starts or resumes a session to store user data

questions.hint: Follow the identifier and server-side state through the stated lifecycle or access check; distinguish client-controlled claims from server decisions.

answer.text: Start or resume PHP session handling and make $_SESSION available.
answer.explanation: WEB29 directly defines session_start() as starting or resuming session handling. The browser normally holds an opaque identifier while server-controlled storage holds the session data. This is separate from a database connection or an HTML form. It does not simply initialize one arbitrary variable, and the server still must validate authorization for protected actions.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Session startup is separate from opening a database connection.

choices.label: B

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: It initializes session handling rather than merely declaring one arbitrary variable.

questions.stem: In CSS, which selector type is denoted by a dot (.)?
questions.hint: Identify which elements a rule targets and distinguish selector syntax from declaration syntax.

answer.explanation: WEB11 defines .notice as a class selector and #logo as an ID selector. The dot is therefore the prefix for a class name, while an element selector uses its type name and grouping uses commas. D correctly identifies the selector category rather than a declaration property or an element’s unique ID.

choices.label: B

questions.stem: What does the SQL AUTO_INCREMENT property do?

options.label: A
options.text: Auto-updates a column when a record is modified

options.label: B
options.text: Generates a unique sequential number for a column

questions.hint: Identify the API and operation first, then distinguish connection setup, statement execution and result processing.

answer.text: Generate automatic numeric values, commonly used for keyed row identifiers; gaps are possible.
answer.explanation: WEB32 says AUTO_INCREMENT generates numeric values and permits gaps or explicit values. B is the intended generated-number description when used with the normal keyed column design, but sequential must not mean gapless business numbering or a promise about every manually supplied value. It does not update arbitrary columns, delete records, or back up the database.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: AUTO_INCREMENT does not automatically update an arbitrary column whenever a record is modified.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: It generates numeric values commonly used for row identifiers; gaps and explicit values remain possible.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: It does not automatically delete old rows.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: It does not perform database backups.

evidence.quote: AUTO_INCREMENT generates numeric values but gaps and explicit values are possible; do not promise gapless consecutive business numbering.

questions.stem: Which PHP function closes a MySQL database connection?
questions.hint: Identify the API and operation first, then distinguish connection setup, statement execution and result processing.

answer.explanation: WEB32 explicitly gives mysqli_close as closing a connection. C names that MySQLi API; the procedural form uses the connection argument in real code. Closing a connection is separate from ending a query or deleting stored data, and the other offered function names are not the standard one identified here.

choices.explanation: mysqli_close closes the MySQLi connection, using its connection argument in procedural code.

PHP, Python, JSP/Java and ASP.NET applications generate server responses and access databases; C# is commonly used with ASP.NET.
Node.js is a JavaScript runtime, not a separate language.

Browser scripts are sandboxed, but may access selected files/devices through permission-based APIs.

A basic static server returns stored files; dynamic processing constructs a representation from logic, requests or data.
Static pages can still run interactive browser scripts, and dynamic generation need not change visible text every time.
A website groups resources; a page is one document/resource.
Open standards do not guarantee identical support for every feature in every browser.
Historical editor-name items refer to Microsoft FrontPage and Macromedia HomeSite5, not languages or required modern tools.

An HTTP/1.1 request begins with method, request-target and version, followed by header fields, a blank line, and an optional body.
For example, GET /courses?id=7 HTTP/1.1 followed by Host: example.edu and a terminating blank line can have no body.
A response begins with version, status code and optional reason phrase, then headers, blank line and permitted content.
Request lines are not response status lines.

Safe describes intended state effects; idempotent means repeating the same request has the same intended effect, not necessarily the same response.
GET/PUT/DELETE are idempotent; arbitrary POST is not.

200 indicates success, 201 creation, 204 success without content, 301 permanent redirection, 400 malformed request, 401 missing/invalid authentication, 403 refusal, 404 unavailable/not found, and 500 an unexpected server failure.

It does not make unvalidated input safe or guarantee a trustworthy merchant.
A RESTful API follows constraints such as client/server separation, stateless requests, cacheability and a uniform resource interface.
Resources have identifiers and representations; JSON is common but not required.
Merely returning JSON does not prove REST.
For a resource /students/7, GET reads it, PUT can replace it, and DELETE requests removal, subject to authentication/authorization and validation.
Represent errors consistently and evaluate retry safety before repeating a request.
Store durable application facts server-side; stateless API requests can still operate on persistent database state.

blocks.text: PDOStatement::rowCount() is a method on a PDO statement object that reports affected rows for its DELETE, INSERT or UPDATE statement. It is not a procedural MySQLi function, and its behavior for SELECT result counts is driver-dependent rather than a portable row-count guarantee.
